key_insight: SciDiagramEdit shows how to automatically edit scientific figures using natural-language instructions, turning paper revision workflows into a machine-learnable task. The key idea is to learn figure edits from real paper revision pairs, where diagrams change across manuscript versions.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the difficulty of automating scientific figure editing during manuscript revision. Unlike simple image editing, scientific diagrams contain mixed elements like plots, labels, arrows, photos, and captions arranged under strict visual and semantic constraints.
method: Build a dataset from scientific paper revision pairs to capture real editing operations on diagrams.
Model the editing task as instruction-guided transformation of complex scientific figures.
Evaluate how well the system can handle common revision actions such as relabeling, rearranging panels, and restyling visual components.
impact: This matters because figure editing is a frequent but time-consuming bottleneck in research publishing. A reliable tool could speed up manuscript revision, reduce manual design work, and help researchers iterate on scientific communication more efficiently.
visual_elements: A pipeline showing input figure + text instruction -> edited output
Icon set for common edits: relabel, move panel, restyle, add/remove element
A dataset or workflow diagram illustrating paper revision pairs
paper_title: SciDiagramEdit: Learning to Edit Scientific Diagrams from Paper Revisions
paper_authors: Yasheng Sun, Zezi Zeng, Yifan Yang, Chong Luo, Wenyi Wang
